'''Finsler's lemma''' is a mathematical result named after [[Paul Finsler]].  It states equivalent ways to express the [[positive definite]]ness of a [[quadratic form]] ''Q'' constrained by a [[linear form]] ''L''. 
Since it is equivalent to another lemmas used in optimization and [[control theory]], such as [[S-procedure|Yakubovich's S-lemma]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zi-Zong|first1=Yan|last2=Jin-Hai|first2=Guo|title=Some Equivalent Results with Yakubovich's S-Lemma|journal=SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization|date=2010|volume=48|issue=7|pages=4474–4480|doi=10.1137/080744219}}</ref> Finsler's lemma has been given many proofs and has been widely used, particularly in results related to [[robust optimization]] and [[Linear matrix inequality|linear matrix inequalities]].

== Statement of Finsler's lemma ==

Let <math>x \in \mathbb{R}^n</math>, and <math>Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}</math> and <math>L \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}</math> be symmetric matrices. The following statements are equivalent:<ref name="Fin:36">{{cite journal|last1=Finsler|first1=Paul|title=Über das Vorkommen definiter und semidefiniter Formen in Scharen quadratischer Formen|journal=[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]|volume=9|issue=1|pages=188–192|doi=10.1007/BF01258188|year=1936|s2cid=121751764 }}</ref>

* <math>\displaystyle x^{T}Lx=0 \text{ and } x \ne 0 \text{ implies } x^T Q x < 0.</math>
* <math>\exists \mu \in \mathbb{R} : Q - \mu L \prec 0. </math>

== Variants ==

=== Non-Strict Finsler Lemma ===
When the matrix ''L'' is indefinite, replacing strict inequalities with non-strict ones still maintains the equivalence between the statements of Finsler's lemma. However, if ''L'' is not indefinite, additional assumptions are necessary to ensure equivalence between the statements.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meijer |first1=Tomas |last2=Scheres |first2=Koen |last3=Eijnden |first3=Sebastiaan van den |last4=Holicki |first4=Tobias |last5=Scherer |first5=Carsten |last6=Heemels |first6=Maurice |date=2024 |title=A Unified Non-Strict Finsler Lemma |journal=IEEE Control Systems Letters |volume=8 |issue=8 |pages=1955–1960 |arxiv=2403.10306 |doi=10.1109/LCSYS.2024.3415473 |bibcode=2024ICSL....8.1955M |issn=2475-1456}}</ref>

=== Extra equivalences when ''L'' is positive semi-definite ===
In the particular case that ''L'' is positive semi-definite, it is possible to decompose it as {{math|1=''L''  = ''B''<sup>T</sup>''B''}}. The following statements, which are also referred as Finsler's lemma in the literature, are equivalent:<ref name="deOS:01">{{cite book |last1=de Oliveira |first1=Maurício C. |url=https://archive.org/details/perspectivesrobu00mohe |title=Perspectives in robust control |last2=Skelton |first2=Robert E. |date=2001 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |isbn=978-1-84628-576-9 |editor1-last=Moheimani |editor1-first=S. O. Reza |location=London |pages=[https://archive.org/details/perspectivesrobu00mohe/page/n248 241]–257 |chapter=Stability tests for constrained linear systems |url-access=limited}}</ref>

* <math> x^T Q x < 0 \text{ for all } x \in \ker(B)\smallsetminus\{0\} </math>
* <math> B^{\perp^T} Q B^\perp \prec 0 </math>
* <math> \exists \mu \in \mathbb{R} : Q - \mu B^T B \prec 0 </math>
* <math> \exists X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m} : Q + XB + B^T X^T \prec 0 </math>

=== Matrix Finsler's lemma ===
There is also a variant of Finsler's lemma for quadratic matrix inequalities, known as '''matrix Finsler's lemma''', which states that the following statements are equivalent for symmetric matrices ''Q'' and ''L'' belonging to '''R'''<sup>(''l''+''k'')x(''l''+''k'')</sup>:<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=van Waarde |first1=Henk J. |last2=Kanat Camlibel |first2=M. |title=2021 60th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC) |chapter=A Matrix Finsler's Lemma with Applications to Data-Driven Control |date=2021-12-14 |chapter-url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9683285 |location=Austin, TX, USA |publisher=IEEE |pages=5777–5782 |doi=10.1109/CDC45484.2021.9683285 |arxiv=2103.13461 |isbn=978-1-6654-3659-5|s2cid=246479914 |url=https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/206606490/A_Matrix_Finslers_Lemma_with_Applications_to_Data_Driven_Control.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=van Waarde |first1=Henk J. |last2=Camlibel |first2=M. Kanat |last3=Eising |first3=Jaap |last4=Trentelman |first4=Harry L. |date=2023-08-31 |title=Quadratic Matrix Inequalities with Applications to Data-Based Control |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/22M1486807 |journal=SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization |language=en |volume=61 |issue=4 |pages=2251–2281 |arxiv=2203.12959 |doi=10.1137/22M1486807 |s2cid=247627787 |issn=0363-0129}}</ref>

* <math> \left[\begin{array}{l}
I \\
Z
\end{array}\right]^{\top} Q\left[\begin{array}{l}
I \\
Z
\end{array}\right] \succeq 0 \text{ for all } Z \in \mathbb{R}^{l \times k} \text { such that }\left[\begin{array}{l}
I \\
Z
\end{array}\right]^{\top} L\left[\begin{array}{l}
I \\
Z
\end{array}\right]=0 </math>
* <math>\exists \mu \in \mathbb{R} : Q - \mu L \succeq 0 </math>

under the assumption that 

<math> Q = \begin{bmatrix}
Q_{11} & Q_{12} \\
Q_{12}^T & Q_{22}
\end{bmatrix} </math> and <math> L = \begin{bmatrix}
L_{11} & L_{12} \\
L_{12}^T & L_{22}
\end{bmatrix} </math>

satisfy the following assumptions:

# ''Q''<sub>12</sub> = 0 and ''Q''<sub>22</sub> < 0,
# ''L''<sub>22</sub> < 0, and ''L''<sub>11</sub> - ''L''<sub>12</sub>''L''<sub>22</sub><sup>+</sup>''L''<sub>12</sub> = 0, and
# there exists a matrix ''G'' such that ''Q''<sub>11</sub> + ''G''<sup>T</sup>''Q''<sub>22</sub>''G'' > 0 and ''L''<sub>22</sub>''G'' = ''L''<sub>12</sub><sup>T</sup><sub>.</sub>

== Generalizations ==

=== Projection lemma ===

The equivalence between the following statements is also common on the literature of [[Linear matrix inequality|linear matrix inequalities]], and is known as the Projection Lemma (or also as Elimination Lemma):<ref>{{Cite book|title=Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory|last1=Boyd|first1=S.|last2=El Ghaoui|first2=L.|last3=Feron|first3=E.|last4=Balakrishnan|first4=V.|date=1994-01-01|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|isbn=9780898714852|series=Studies in Applied and Numerical Mathematics|doi=10.1137/1.9781611970777|s2cid=27307648 }}</ref>
* <math> B^{\perp^T} Q B^\perp \prec 0 \text{ and } C^{T \perp T} Q C^{T \perp} \prec 0 </math> 
* <math> \exists X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m} : Q + CXB + B^T X^T C^T \prec 0 </math>
This lemma generalizes one of the Finsler's lemma variants by including an extra matrix ''C'' and an extra constraint involving this extra matrix. 

It is interesting to note that if the strict inequalities are changed to non-strict inequalities, the equivalence does not hold anymore: only the second statement imply the first statement. Nevertheless, it still possible to obtain the equivalence between the statements under extra assumptions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meijer |first1=T. J. |last2=Holicki |first2=T. |last3=Eijnden |first3=S. J. A. M. van den |last4=Scherer |first4=C. W. |last5=Heemels |first5=W. P. M. H. |date=2024 |title=The Non-Strict Projection Lemma |journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control |volume=69 |issue=8 |pages=5584–5590 |arxiv=2305.08735 |doi=10.1109/TAC.2024.3371374 |bibcode=2024ITAC...69.5584M |issn=0018-9286}}</ref>

=== Robust version ===
Finsler's lemma also generalizes for matrices ''Q'' and ''B'' depending on a parameter ''s'' within a set ''S''. In this case, it is natural to ask if the same variable μ (respectively ''X'') can satisfy <math>Q(s)-\mu B^{T}(s)B(s) \prec 0</math> for all <math>s\in S</math> (respectively, <math>Q(s) + X(s)B(s)+B^T(s)X^T(s) \prec 0</math>). If ''Q'' and ''B'' depends continuously on the parameter ''s'', and ''S'' is [[Compact car|compact]], then this is true. If ''S'' is not compact, but ''Q'' and ''B'' are still continuous matrix-valued functions, then μ and ''X'' can be guaranteed to be at least continuous functions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ishihara|first1=J. Y.|last2=Kussaba|first2=H. T. M.|last3=Borges|first3=R. A.|date=August 2017|title=Existence of Continuous or Constant Finsler's Variables for Parameter-Dependent Systems|journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control|volume=62|issue=8|pages=4187–4193|doi=10.1109/tac.2017.2682221|issn=0018-9286|arxiv=1711.04570|bibcode=2017ITAC...62.4187I |s2cid=20563439 }}</ref>

== Applications ==

=== Data-driven control ===
The matrix variant of Finsler lemma has been applied to the data-driven control of Lur'e systems<ref name=":0" /> and in a data-driven robust linear matrix inequality-based model predictive control scheme.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Nguyen |first1=Hoang Hai |last2=Friedel |first2=Maurice |last3=Findeisen |first3=Rolf |date=2023-03-08 |title=LMI-based Data-Driven Robust Model Predictive Control |class=eess.SY |eprint=2303.04777 }}</ref>

=== S-Variable approach to robust control of linear dynamical systems ===
Finsler's lemma can be used to give novel linear matrix inequality (LMI) characterizations to stability and control problems.<ref name="deOS:01" /> The set of LMIs stemmed from this procedure yields less conservative results when applied to control problems where the system matrices has dependence on a parameter, such as [[robust control]] problems and control of linear-parameter varying systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Oliveira|first1=R. C. L. F.|last2=Peres|first2=P. L. D.|date=July 2007|title=Parameter-Dependent LMIs in Robust Analysis: Characterization of Homogeneous Polynomially Parameter-Dependent Solutions Via LMI Relaxations|journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control|volume=52|issue=7|pages=1334–1340|doi=10.1109/tac.2007.900848|bibcode=2007ITAC...52.1334O |s2cid=23352506 |issn=0018-9286}}</ref> This approach has recently been called as S-variable approach<ref>{{Cite book|title=S-Variable Approach to LMI-Based Robust Control {{!}} SpringerLink|last1=Ebihara|first1=Yoshio|last2=Peaucelle|first2=Dimitri|last3=Arzelier|first3=Denis|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-1-4471-6606-1|series = Communications and Control Engineering|year = 2015|isbn = 978-1-4471-6605-4}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hosoe|first1=Y.|last2=Peaucelle|first2=D.|title=2016 European Control Conference (ECC) |chapter=S-variable approach to robust stabilization state feedback synthesis for systems characterized by random polytopes |date=June 2016|pages=2023–2028|doi=10.1109/ecc.2016.7810589|isbn=978-1-5090-2591-6|s2cid=34083031 }}</ref> and the LMIs stemming from this approach are known as SV-LMIs (also known as dilated LMIs<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Ebihara|first1=Y.|last2=Hagiwara|first2=T.|title=Proceedings of the 41st SICE Annual Conference. SICE 2002 |chapter=A dilated LMI approach to robust performance analysis of linear time-invariant uncertain systems |date=August 2002|volume=4|pages=2585–2590 vol.4|doi=10.1109/sice.2002.1195827|isbn=978-0-7803-7631-1|s2cid=125985256 }}</ref>).

=== Sufficient condition for universal stabilizability of non-linear systems ===
A [[nonlinear system]] has the universal stabilizability property if every forward-complete solution of a system can be globally stabilized. By the use of Finsler's lemma, it is possible to derive a sufficient condition for universal stabilizability in terms of a differential linear matrix inequality.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Manchester|first1=I. R.|last2=Slotine|first2=J. J. E.|date=June 2017|title=Control Contraction Metrics: Convex and Intrinsic Criteria for Nonlinear Feedback Design|journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control|volume=62|issue=6|pages=3046–3053|doi=10.1109/tac.2017.2668380|issn=0018-9286|arxiv=1503.03144|bibcode=2017ITAC...62.3046M |s2cid=5100489 }}</ref>
